request.spec:
A change that alters any person's overdue-total is now also followed by the rollup lines, and
every ROLLUP line gains overdue-total=<overdue-total> at its end, every TOTALS line
overdue-total=<total> at its end (a TOTALS line is written when any of its three totals moved).
A change of the sheet's today that puts a claim past its due-by, or takes one out of overdue, is
such a change even when no due or due-total moved.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A change that alters any person's overdue-total is now also followed by the rollup lines, and
every ROLLUP line gains overdue-total=<overdue-total> at its end, every TOTALS line
overdue-total=<total> at its end (a TOTALS line is written when any of its three totals moved).
A change of the sheet's today that puts a claim past its due-by, or takes one out of overdue, is
such a change even when no due or due-total moved.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The change is in, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

Every ROLLUP line now ends with `overdue-total=<person's overdue-total>`, and every TOTALS line ends with `overdue-total=<sheet's overdue-total>`. A change that only moves someone's overdue-total now writes these lines too. A TOTALS line is written when any of its three totals moves.

The whole change is in one file, `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/rollup/RollupService.java`:

- **Working out overdue-total:** it is calculated the same way the screen already does it. It adds up the dues of the person's counted claims that are OPEN or PENDING and past their due-by (claims with no rate are skipped), and it is not held to the sheet's cap.
- **Writing the lines:** a person gets a ROLLUP line if their claimed, due-total or overdue-total moved.
- **Changing the sheet's today:** this already went through the same check. So moving today so that a claim becomes overdue, or stops being overdue, now writes ROLLUP and TOTALS lines even when no due moved.

The front end, the stored data and the database schema didn't need changing, because the screen already showed overdue totals.
